text:
chris: Hey support — since ~09:00 UTC we've been getting intermittent 502/504 on the hosted /v1/generate endpoint. Example response: `502 Bad Gateway`, request_id=abc123xyz, timestamp=2026-03-15T09:12:34Z. Affects eu-west-1 and us-west-2, roughly 3-7% of requests in the last 20m. Using SDK v1.4.2 (node). Can you help? This is impacting a paying customer flow.

sara: thanks — sorry about this. are you on Redwood Hosted (api.redwood.ai) or a Dedicated deployment?

chris: Hosted (api.redwood.ai). SDK v1.4.2, default retry settings. We saw the errors in production traces and in our app logs. I can paste a curl repro and a sample response.

chris: curl repro (redacted API key):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"hi"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response:
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:34 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":{"message":"upstream read timeout","code":502},"request_id":"abc123xyz"}
```

sara: copying to eng-oncall — @mike can you triage? chris, can you also share approximate RPS and token sizes when this was happening?

mike: oncall looking. @chris, can you DM me the full request_id(s)? I'll start pulling traces. Also what model and max_tokens did you set?

chris: DM sent with a few request_ids: abc123xyz, def456uvw. Model was gpt-large, max_tokens=1024, typical prompt length ~300 tokens. Peak RPS ~ 120 for the route, bursts to ~300 for ~30s windows.

mike: got them. initial trace shows runtime returned a 504/upstream timeout at approx 30s in the request path; the runtime's front proxy then translated to 502 for some requests. Looking at metrics, there was a spike in request queue length at 09:09-09:13 and error rates for the model worker rose concurrently.

infra-bot: [09:09:48] autoscaler-controller: Failed to scale up: FailedCreatePod: InsufficientInstanceCapacity in eu-west-1 (node group pool-rt-g4dn)

deepa: platform chiming in — we just noticed an instance-type capacity shortage in eu-west-1 for the G4-like machine type. Autoscaler attempted to add nodes but got InsufficientInstanceCapacity. Kube events around 09:08-09:11 show `FailedCreatePod` and `CreateContainerConfigError` for some pods.

deepa: relevant k8s event snippet:
```
9:08:52 FailedCreatePod pod/worker-7c8d9 0/10 nodes are available: Insufficient cpu, InsufficientInstanceCapacity.
9:10:03 Backoff restarting failed container
```

mike: that explains the queueing + timeouts. model workers couldn't scale to meet burst. For some requests the model exec exceeded upstream timeout (30s). Two mitigations: 1) manual scale the pool to drain backlog, 2) route affected customers to a different region or to a smaller model variant while we resolve capacity.

sara: chris — would you be able to accept a temporary route to us-west-2 or to `gpt-medium` for the next 30m? We can also apply a manual capacity bump immediately.

chris: prefer us-west-2 if that's fastest. We can switch on our side if you provide endpoint/region guidance. Customer impact is mainly slow increases in latency and a few failed requests — they prefer no model quality drop but will accept region fallback if it reduces errors.

deepa: manual scale initiated: adding 10 pods to runtime pool in eu-west-1. Also opening a ticket with cloud provider to request extra capacity in the short term.

infra-bot: [09:19:12] manual-scale: +10 pods to pool-rt-g4dn by deepa (request id: scale-789)

mike: monitoring queue. current backlog 850 -> 120 in 6m and dropping. Error rate on /v1/generate dropping.

sara: update for customer: we've applied a temporary capacity bump in eu-west-1 which has begun draining the backlog. We also offered an option to route to us-west-2 — chris opted to try us-west-2 for a subset of requests. Will follow up with a status update in 30 minutes. :white_check_mark:

lia: CS note — I messaged the customer's ops lead and told them we've applied a mitigation (manual scale) and recommended a regional fallback. Customer asked for ETA for full resolution.

mike: root cause summary so far: cloud instance shortage prevented autoscaler from provisioning new capacity during a traffic burst, which caused model workers to backlog and some upstream timeouts (30s). Immediate fix = manual scale bump + regional routing. Long term: autoscaler should be resilient to partial capacity errors and fallback to alternate instance types or regions.

sara: chris to confirm — after switching a subset of traffic to us-west-2, are you still seeing 502s for the routed traffic?

chris: so far so good on us-west-2 subset (ran for 12m), no 502s. EU traffic reduced errors after scale. We'll keep monitoring and send any further traces.

mike: action items:
- platform: follow up with cloud provider to secure more capacity and add fallback instance types (deepa)
- eng/runtime: evaluate increasing internal upstream timeout or better backpressure signalling (mike)
- support/CS: send customer-facing timeline and RCA draft in 2-4 hours (sara/lia)
- SDK team: recommend default retry/backoff changes for bursty clients and publish guidance (sara -> sdk)

deepa: opened provider ticket and requested capacity reservation; also adding alternate instance types to autoscaler config as a temp measure. Will update here when provider confirms.

infra-bot: [09:51:08] provider-ticket: CREATED ticket#CP-4457 — awaiting provider response

mike: quick client guidance we gave chris: increase retry initial delay to 500-1000ms with exponential backoff and jitter, cap retries to 4 for 502/504 on generate endpoints to avoid thundering herd. Also consider using smaller max_tokens or streaming responses.

sara: final immediate status: backlog drained, error rate back to baseline for now. Keeping thread open until provider response and we prepare a short RCA draft. Thanks everyone. :rotating_light:

chris: thanks team — appreciate the quick action. We'll keep an eye and will reach out if anything spikes again.

lia: I'll send the customer update now and include estimated timeline for RCA (aiming EOD).

mike: filing a short postmortem template entry now and will link provider ticket and autoscaler events. Follow-ups: autoscaler robustness and runtime upstream timeout tuning.

sara: closing note: if chris sees any recurring 5xx after today, please re-open and we'll escalate to higher priority. Thanks all.
